In similar retrieved cases, the answers referenced a kidney-specific finding or a normal-appearing abdomen, but those cases are not reliable for this image and should only be taken as general context for what to inspect.

key_facts: Normal kidneys are usually bean-shaped, symmetric, and located in the retroperitoneum on either side of the spine.
The renal cortex should have fairly smooth outer contours without focal masses, marked scarring, or distortion.
The collecting system should not be dilated in a normal study; hydronephrosis suggests obstruction.
Perinephric fat stranding, renal stones, cysts, or masses are common CT abnormalities.
Comparison of both kidneys helps detect asymmetry in size, enhancement, or contour.
